units: <cite ref="Mishnah Negaim 12:6">Neg. XII, 6</cite> <he>שניהן … קוֹצְעִין</he> both neighbors must bear the expense for tearing out (the leprous stone) and for scraping (the wall); Sifra M’tsorʿa, Neg., Par. 6, ch. IV; a. e.
<cite ref="Taanit 28a:7">Taan. 28ᵃ</cite> <he>קוֹצְעֵי קציעית</he> those pretending to be engaged in packing figs; Tosef. ib. IV (III), 7 (Var. <he>קוֹצְאֵי</he>); Y. ib. IV, 68ᵇ bot.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 27:4">Kel. XXVII, 4</cite> <he>המְקַצֵּע מכולם וכ׳</he> if in trimming any of them he cuts off a piece one handbreadth square.

<cite ref="Zevachim 94a:4">Zeb. 94ᵃ</cite> <he>עוצבא … לקַצְּעָהּ … עד שיְקַצְּעֶנָּה</he> a fur intended to be trimmed (v. <cite ref="P00644"><he>עיּצְבָּא</he></cite>) remains unsusceptible of uncleanness until it has been trimmed; <cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 4:10">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. IV, 10</cite>.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 66b:11">B. Kam. 66ᵇ</cite> <he>כגון שקִיצְּעָן</he> (Ar. <he>שקצען</he>) when he trimmed the stolen furs.

<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 11:8">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. XI, 8</cite> <he>אם היה גדול וקִיצְּעוֹ</he> (not <he>וקיצעו</he>) if the cloth was large and he shortened it by trimming; <cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 11:9">ib. 9</cite>.
<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 11:2">Ib. 2</cite> <he>עד שיְקַצֵּעַ</he> (or <he>שיִקְצַע</he>) until he cuts off (the defective portion).
<cite ref="Chullin 123b:15">Ḥull. 123ᵇ</cite> <he>במקצע ובא לו וכ׳</he> when he trimmed (the skin) going all around; a. e.
